newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse trade lower as Dow falls.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse trade lower as Dow falls.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade slightly lower on Wednesday as the overnight weakness of the U.S. Dow Jones index outweighed the positive effect of a strong dollar against the mark.

The DAX index of Germany's 30 leading shares fell 4.33 points, or 0.17 percent, to 2,566.62 in early trade on small volumes as dealers said there were renewed concerns about an early U.S. interest rate increase.

"Shares are only moving sideways at the moment, there's a lot of uncertainty and 2,570 points is being seen as a point of resistance," said one dealer, noting that the strength of the dollar was nonetheless providing stability.
The U.S. currency traded at about 1.5130 in morning dealings, just higher than late Tuesday European levels, with the underlying tone seen to be positive.

But dealers said the mood of uncertainty was set to intensify from tomorrow onwards ahead of a raft of U.S. data due on Thursday and Friday which could be taken as a possible influence on U.S. interest rates.

"We've only got the Beige Book (on the U.S. economy at 1600 GMT) today which isn't expected to yield much but concern will start making itself felt more from tomorrow," one said, noting the publication of U.S. August producer prices on Thursday.
The latest U.S. money supply data is also due late Thursday, with August consumer prices and retail sales figures in the U.S. due Friday.
Export-led stocks such as those in the chemical sector showed muted gains despite the higher dollar.
Hoechst AG, up 30 pfennigs to 53.30 marks, and Bayer AG, up 64 pfennigs at 54.57, were among the strongest DAX-30 shares.

Deutsche Bank AG continued to suffer from the problems at its London-based Morgan Grenfell asset management unit, with its shares hitting a low of 71.25 marks before recovering slightly to 71.35, 15 pfennigs down on the day.
